answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments, instantiated via a copper-based kernel, enable verifiable reputation sorting, where agents employ verifiable delay primitives to maintain a mirror-like consistency of their participation history, rendering identity cloning computationally infeasible. Through staking collateral and slashing penalties, the system incentivizes honest behavior, thereby establishing a robust Nash equilibrium, which negates the expected utility of malicious attacks, ultimately guaranteeing the resilience of the network against Sybil attacks.
